test_positive_central_charge_scaling.description: cvc5 SAT: R_large > R_small implies c_large > c_small (c ∝ R)

test_boundary_brown_henneaux.statement: Central charge c in boundary CFT relates to 2D gravity on AdS via c = (3R/2G). R is AdS radius, G is Newton constant in 3D gravity.
test_boundary_brown_henneaux.consequence: Central charge is entirely determined by bulk geometry; no other free parameters. Duality requires c > 0 always.
test_boundary_brown_henneaux.application: For large c: weakly coupled CFT (gravity classical limit). For small c: strongly coupled CFT. Phase transitions occur at c critical points.

test_boundary_virasoro_cft.statement: Central charge c appears in Virasoro commutation: [L_m, L_n] = (m-n)L_{m+n} + (c/12)(m³-m)δ_{m,-n}. In 2D CFT, anomaly term (c/12) is the central extension.
test_boundary_virasoro_cft.consequence: c quantizes conformal symmetry; it is a topological invariant of the CFT (cannot change without phase transition). Equals (number of field DOFs) for free CFT.
test_boundary_virasoro_cft.application: Free scalar: c=1. Free fermion: c=1/2. WZW k level: c = k·dim(G)/(k+C_G). Cosets reduce c.

test_boundary_conformal_anomaly.description: cvc5 SAT: Conformal anomaly scales as (c/12)/R² with c = (3R/2G)
